clue.text: The state of one love had rejected

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: rejected means the word had is turned back to front

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover's rejection seems to be the topic, with someone spurning a love they once had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The state' could seem a condition, but it is a US state; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Converts apt in time to get restless

indicators.note: converts signals that the letters of the following words are changed into another form

explanation.surface: Someone converting an apartment over time grows impatient with the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converts' rearranges the nine letters of APT IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient is a synonym: someone restless cannot bear waiting.

clue.text: Concerning the sailor away from home

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
someone away from home is out

explanation.surface: A remark about a sailor who is away from home on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: About and concerning are synonyms as prepositions, both meaning on the subject of.

clue.text: The players presenting gold 'box to a painter

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a chest is a large box
RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

explanation.surface: Someone presents a golden box to an artist as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is the body of musicians who play together, so the players.

clue.text: Well-known artist swindles the board!

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks
a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a plank on legs

explanation.surface: A famous painter is accused of cheating the company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the board' looks like a company's directors; here it is simply a table. John Constable was an English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable is the celebrated English painter of The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Trick that's really smart — an eye-opener

parts.note: chic means stylish, very smart in dress
taken as written

indicators.note: an eye-opener read literally is the letter that opens the word eye

explanation.surface: A clever ruse is praised as both stylish and revealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opener' looks like a surprise; it is just the first letter of eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicane is a piece of trickery or chicanery, a deception.

clue.text: Old-fashioned wants.

parts.note: an archaic third-person form of the verb meaning requires, as in the King James Bible

explanation.surface: A plain description of desires that are out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: The -eth ending is the archaic third-person singular, so this is the old way of saying he requires.

clue.text: A drinking man upset about a heroine of opera

indicators.note: upset means the word for a drunkard is turned over, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A drunk is upset over the fate of an operatic heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the title heroine of Puccini's opera, a singer who leaps to her death.

clue.text: Looking for scraps?

parts.note: scraps read as fights rather than leftovers, so the phrase describes someone spoiling for a fight

explanation.surface: A hungry animal seems to be searching for leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means aggressive and eager to fight, just like a person spoiling for a scrap.

clue.text: Seeing a bit of grey in golden hair

indicators.note: a bit of says only a short run of the following words is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone notices a grey strand among golden locks.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across grEY IN Golden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying is a spelling of eyeing, meaning looking at or watching.

clue.text: Denounce plagiarism in plain language

indicators.note: in says the copying word goes inside the word for plain writing

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, not verse
a crib is a copied piece of work

explanation.surface: A critic condemns copying and says so in plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to condemn or forbid something formally.

clue.text: Sarah on the motorway in quite a stew

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sarah
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the digit read as I

explanation.surface: Sarah, driving on the motorway, is getting into a real state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in quite a stew' looks like Sarah's agitation; it is the dish. The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich ragout of game birds, so a kind of stew.

clue.text: It must be returned by the tenth

indicators.note: returned means the little word It is sent back, written in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An item must be handed back by the tenth of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the church.

clue.text: Getting to the mean state — getting old

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
aging means growing older

explanation.surface: Someone describes reaching a middling, elderly state of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Averaging is working out or arriving at the arithmetic mean.

clue.text: The letter pile set in order

indicators.note: putting things in order here means arranging the letters of pile set properly

explanation.surface: Someone sorts a pile of correspondence into order.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, especially a formal one like those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Get in Lane' order may appear rude

indicators.note: an order to get into lane is reread as putting the letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A traffic instruction to get in lane might come across as discourteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, close to rude in the sense of rough and unpolished.

clue.text: The ghost of Hamlet's father made the night this

definitions.text: The ghost of Hamlet's father made the night this

parts.words: The ghost of Hamlet's father made the night this
parts.note: Hamlet asks why the ghost comes, making night so ghastly, in his words to it in Act 1

explanation.surface: A question about the effect of the ghost in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says to his father's ghost that it comes 'making night hideous'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Shakespeare uses means frightful or horrible, describing the ghastly night.

clue.text: Underworld king giving-a cleric shelter and board

indicators.note: giving shelter says the god holds the priest inside him

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: The underworld's ruler takes in a clergyman, offering lodging and meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like food as in board and lodging; it is a company's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: The directors of a company together form its board.

clue.text: Veronica's rate of progress is satisfactory

parts.note: speed is the rate at which progress is made
well can mean all right, satisfactory

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica is told her progress is going nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name; it is the plant genus, and the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the botanical name of the blue-flowered plant genus commonly called by this name.

clue.text: All of these people walk in London

explanation.surface: A remark about a crowd strolling through the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as THEM ALL for everyone here; THE MALL is the avenue leading to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means every one of them; as a name it is the processional road running from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Mid-evening in the days before Easter, can be mild

indicators.note: in says the central letters go inside the season's name

parts.note: Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: mid- takes the central letters of evening, dropping the outer pairs

explanation.surface: In the middle of an evening in the period before Easter, things may be gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid-' takes ENI, the middle three letters of evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means merciful and gentle in judgment, soft rather than severe.

clue.text: Get back into heart and train

indicators.note: into says the reversed word goes inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

indicators.note: back says the word Get is written in reverse

explanation.surface: An instruction to return to the heart of something and practise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TEG, which goes into CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession, a train of mourners following the coffin.

clue.text: Lead may be found in beastly food = sweet sauce

indicators.note: may be found in says the performer is placed inside the animal food

parts.note: cud is the food cattle chew again
the star is the leading performer

explanation.surface: A warning that the toxic metal can turn up in animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal; it is the star of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet sauce made from milk, eggs and sugar, poured over puddings.

clue.text: Trumpeters who use trunks for their effects

definitions.text: Trumpeters who use trunks for their effects

parts.words: Trumpeters who use trunks for their effects
parts.note: the trumpeting animals use their long noses, not luggage trunks for belongings

explanation.surface: Musicians who pack their belongings in luggage trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: These huge animals trumpet loudly through their long proboscises.

clue.text: Odd characters lend a buck

indicators.note: odd characters suggests the letters of lend a are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Some eccentric people lend a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck' looks like a dollar; it is a male antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope, and a buck is the male of such an animal.

clue.text: Poor actor about fifty with a game to play

indicators.note: about says the bad performer goes around the numeral

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting performer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad actor of about fifty has a part in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game for two or four players, played with pegs or counters.

clue.text: Press — what a lot of them!

explanation.surface: Journalists swarming in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a throng of people, and a large number of them gathered together is a throng too.

clue.text: Love to scold and hold forth

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold angrily

explanation.surface: Someone who loves to nag and lecture people.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a long speech, holding forth pompously.

clue.text: Benefit from a sound screen

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sound says we hear the word for a concealing cloth rather than see it

parts.note: a veil is a screen that hides something

explanation.surface: Someone gains from a soundproof screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail is advantage or use, as in to no avail.

clue.text: When broken down, are able to provide further details

indicators.note: broken down suggests the letters of are able to are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: People who break down are still able to explain themselves further.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to expand on something by adding more detail.

clue.text: Action taken about a plot of: land that's depreciated

indicators.note: about says the deed is placed around the area of land

parts.note: a deed is an action that has been done
a tract is an area or plot of land

explanation.surface: Legal action over a piece of land has lowered its value.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the clue is a printing stray.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to belittle or disparage, so depreciated in the sense of run down.

clue.text: The interval — magic words!

explanation.surface: An intermission in a magic show.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of time, and also an incantation of charmed words.
